name: llama.cpp server (Vulkan GPU)
purpose: One llama.cpp HTTP server (OpenAI-compatible /v1 API, /health, built-in chat page) for one GGUF model, run as a non-root container on the host's GPU through its Vulkan render node. The model directory comes from an existing read-only dataset (bind it with --dataset models=/abs/dir). One model uses most of the VRAM, so every instance on a host holds the same exclusive GPU resource: only one runs at a time (deploy switch-plan moves it). No authentication: anyone who can reach the claimed address and port can use the model.

parameters.description: Directory of the model inside the models dataset, for example unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF; only this directory is mounted, read-only, at /models.
GGUF file inside model-dir, for example Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf (the first part of a split model).
Further llama-server arguments, space-separated tokens without quotes (GPU layers, flash attention, KV cache types, parallel slots, speculative decoding).

devices.description: The GPU's DRM render node: Vulkan compute and GPU memory, no display output (no card node).

identities.name: /dev/dri/renderD128
identities.description: LLM slot of the GPU, shared with Ollama: one model needs most of the GPU's memory, so at most one holder runs (start, unfence and plans refuse while another holds it; deploy switch-plan moves it).

identities.name: /dev/dri/renderD128 image slot
identities.description: Image slot of the GPU, shared with ComfyUI: a llama.cpp server also excludes ComfyUI, while Ollama (LLM slot only) and ComfyUI (image slot only) may run together and take turns on VRAM.

consumers: No authentication: every host that can reach this address and port can send prompts and use the API and chat page
Browsers (the chat page needs gzip; curl needs --compressed)

capacity.gpu: Vulkan-capable GPU render node (Mesa RADV on the RX 7900 XTX); VRAM for the chosen model and context (27B Q4_K_XL at 64K q8_0 KV: about 19-20 GB)

evidence: The image runs /app/llama-server as its entrypoint; the tag's digest is resolved at plan time and pinned in the instance
